goal: Replace TaPEx placeholder with a real HuggingFace transformers wrapper (microsoft/tapex-base-finetuned-wtq) so QA-eval comparisons are no longer distorted by a constant-response stub.
verified: Pre-iteration: run_tape_placeholder always returned [C5]; iteration 5's eval record explicitly flagged baselines_are_placeholders: true.
After iteration: TaPExBaseline lazy-loads the HF transformers pipeline only on first .answer() call; injecting pipeline= in tests bypasses any network/model download.

Wrapper correctly extracts table from workbook range, builds {column: [cells]} dict, disambiguates duplicate header strings (caught by a test that initially failed and forced the dict-construction rewrite), wraps answer in [...] to match the paper's QA contract.
run_qa_evaluation.py exposes --real-tapex / --tapex-model flags; when --real-tapex is on, per_question records the answer under 'tapex_real' and out_record sets tapex_kind='real'.
Backward-compatible: --real-tapex omitted -> placeholder path retained, eval record carries tapex_kind='placeholder' and baselines_are_placeholders: true.
inferred: TaPEx requires string-keyed columns; we synthesize A/B/C headers when the first row is all-numeric so the wrapper degrades gracefully on header-less tables.
Holding off on Binder integration — Binder is research-grade neural-symbolic SQL; vendor it as iteration 7+ rather than bundling here.
unknown: Whether on real spreadsheet QA datasets the synthesized-header fallback and 64-row truncation cap distort accuracy enough to misrepresent TaPEx's true performance. Will need a real benchmark run (gated on user's environment + GPU) to verify.
